THIS ROLE IS ON-SITE IN SCHAKELFORT, TEXAS (NO EXCEPTION). RELOCATION ASSISTANCE IS AVAILABLE.
Key Responsibilities
- Lead daily operations, maintenance, and service execution for critical mechanical and HVAC infrastructure.

- Own mechanical plant readiness, including preventive maintenance, corrective work, inspections, restoration activities, and maintenance backlog management.

- Serve as the primary site point of contact and technical lead for mechanical systems, including incident escalation and operational decision support.

- Manage Facilities Technicians, contractors, and service vendors, ensuring strong safety performance, quality of work, documentation rigor, and SLA adherence.

- Drive troubleshooting and response for mechanical failures, abnormal conditions, and performance degradation impacting uptime or operational stability.

- Track and improve KPIs such as equipment availability, backlog health, MTTR, repeat failures, maintenance completion, and corrective action closure.

- Partner with engineering, commissioning, deployment, reliability, and controls teams on retrofits, upgrades, system turnover, and operational acceptance.

- Lead or support root cause analysis for major or recurring issues and ensure corrective actions are fully implemented, verified, and sustained.

- Maintain audit-ready records including procedures, service reports, maintenance history, turnover documentation, and CMMS data.

- Champion safe work practices, environmental compliance, and disciplined process execution across all mechanical operations.

- Coach and develop technicians and frontline leads to strengthen troubleshooting capability, technical depth, and execution consistency.

- Support the Site Operations Director with status reporting, risk visibility, staffing readiness, and operational improvement initiatives for the mechanical plant.

Qualifications
- 5–8 years of experience in mechanical plant operations, HVAC service, critical cooling maintenance, or related uptime-critical environments such as data centers, healthcare, industrial plants, semiconductor, or large commercial facilities.
- 1–3+ years of experience leading technicians, maintenance teams, or service providers in a live operational environment.
- Strong knowledge of chilled water systems, cooling towers, pumps, CRAHs, AHUs, CDUs, and related controls platforms.
- Experience managing vendors, maintenance programs, incident response, and service execution in 24x7 operations.
- Familiarity with BMS, SCADA, DCIM, and CMMS tools.
- Experience supporting commissioning, turnover, or operational acceptance of new or upgraded mechanical systems is preferred.

Skills and Competencies
- Strong troubleshooting judgment and calm decision-making under pressure.

- Deep commitment to safety, procedure adherence, and documentation rigor.

- Clear communicator able to translate plant conditions, risks, and actions for varied stakeholders.

- Strong planning and execution discipline across maintenance, backlog, and operational priorities.

- Ability to lead technicians and vendors while reinforcing accountability and consistent field execution.

Preferred Skills / Certifications
- Experience with mission-critical cooling infrastructure and redundancy strategies in high-availability environments.

- Familiarity with predictive maintenance, trend analysis, controls integration, and operational performance monitoring.

- EPA Section 608 Certification preferred where refrigerant-handling responsibilities apply.

- HVAC trade license, mechanical certification, or equivalent technical qualification where applicable.

- OEM or manufacturer training on chillers, cooling systems, pumps, cooling towers, CRAH/CRAC systems, or related controls platforms preferred.

- OSHA 30 preferred.

Physical Demands / Work Environment
This is a mission-critical onsite role supporting 24/7 operations where continuous uptime is essential; as such, regular attendance, schedule flexibility, and response readiness are required. To perform these duties, you must be able to frequently walk, bend, kneel, crouch, push/pull objects, and climb stairs. You may be required to lift or move up to 39 pounds independently and participate in group lifts for loads 40 pounds or greater. You must also be capable of maintaining balance while working from ladders or elevated platforms. These tasks are performed in an industrial environment and must be executed safely, with or without reasonable accommodation, to maintain the continuous health of facility infrastructure.
Why Oracle Cloud Infrastructure?
Global impact at scale: Contribute directly to how mission-critical OCI data centers operate across regions and continents, influencing infrastructure reliability, security, sustainability, and long-term capacity growth.
Technically rigorous environment: Work alongside experienced engineers, automation specialists, and compliance teams in a rapidly scaling hyperscale cloud infrastructure, where disciplined execution and technical depth matter.
Culture built on operational excellence: Join an organization that values safety, process rigor, clear accountability, and continuous improvement as foundational to protecting uptime and customer trust.
Long-term career development: Benefit from internal mobility, role-based technical training, and development opportunities designed for professionals building long-term careers in cloud infrastructure and facilities operations.

jobs.title: Data Center Facilities Operations manager
jobs.description:
As a data center facilities Operations manager, you will independently support the reliability, efficiency, and lifecycle performance of mission-critical mechanical, electrical, CCTV, Fire protection (SSPI), Access control system, and HVAC (heating, ventilation, and air conditioning) systems essential to the smooth operation of hyperscale data centers.

In this role, you will apply strong technical knowledge of data center infrastructure management and, more broadly, of redundancy strategies and operational risks to maintain the long-term availability and performance of the systems.

You will participate in incident management and root cause analysis, contribute to maintenance planning and commissioning activities, and identify opportunities to improve the reliability, maintainability, and efficiency of technical systems.
Career Level - IC4
Key Responsibilities

- Independently, in collaboration with the COLO, ensure the monitoring and control of operations, inspections, maintenance, and troubleshooting of mechanical, electrical, HVAC, CCTV, and SSPI systems…

- Perform advanced troubleshooting, investigate incidents, respond to alarms, and coordinate with the COLO to carry out root cause analyses for issues related to equipment or other operational systems in the data center environment.

- Support and improve maintenance procedures, operational sequences, diagrams, P&IDs, SLD’s, documentation quality, and operational standards.

- Assist with capacity planning, upgrades, equipment replacements, commissioning activities, acceptance tests, and operational transfer requirements carried out by the COLO.

- Work with on-site operations teams to improve maintainability, work safety, reliability, efficiency, and outcomes throughout the data center environment lifecycle.

- Coordinate with COLO teams, service providers, internal engineering teams, and operations stakeholders to support maintenance, repairs, testing, and system upgrades.

- Use the building management system (BMS), control platforms, alarms, trends, and maintenance data to assess system performance, identify recurring issues, and recommend corrective actions to the COLO

- Review and keep the technical documentation of the sites up to date, including maintenance records, drawings, P&IDs, sequences of operation, and supplier documentation to ensure consistent execution across all sites.

- Promote operational safety, compliance with environmental standards, awareness of the safety of people and property

Skills and Competencies

- Strong understanding of the facility’s components and their operating parameters.

- Detailed knowledge of data center operating environments and the four key constraints on operational efficiency (power, cooling, IT, and space), as well as the necessary operational policies, procedures, and compliance requirements based on legislation, standards (national and international), and codes of conduct.

- Good operational judgment in the event of alarms, abnormal situations, maintenance activities, and high-risk operational scenarios.

- Strong sense of responsibility and accountability in day-to-day operations.

- Clear communication of technical issues, findings, corrective actions, and operational risks.

- Strong safety mindset and strict adherence to procedures, lockout/tagout measures, and safe work practices.

- Ability to analyze system trends, alarm history, and maintenance logs to identify opportunities for improvement.

- Strong coordination skills when collaborating with the COLO, on-site operations teams, engineering teams, and service providers.

Preferred Skills / Certifications

- Experience with chillers, pumps, cooling towers, CRAH/CRAC units, heat exchangers.

- Experience with power distribution systems, substations, SWB, busways..

- Experience with low-voltage systems, CCTV, access control systems, SSPI fire safety systems...

- Familiarity with BMS, PLC/controls concepts, sequences of operation, trending, alarm management, commissioning, and vendor coordination.

- Experience supporting maintenance planning, acceptance testing, energy-efficiency projects, equipment change-outs, and operational handover.

- Have a DEV OPS mindset, and the ability to code is desirable.

- ASHRAE training

- Uptime Institute training, AOS (Accredited Operations Specialist), CDCMP (Certified Data Center Management Professional), Certified Data Center Technician Professional ( CDCTP ®) or similar data center infrastructure training

Physical Demands / Work Environment

- This is a mission-critical role supporting 24/7 operations where 100% uptime is essential; as such, regular attendance and flexibility for shift-based schedules are required.

- The position is based in an industrial environment and must be executed safely, with or without reasonable accommodation, to maintain the continuous health of the facility infrastructure.

jobs.title: Data Center Operations Lead ( Kuala Lumpur/ Johor Bahru)
jobs.description:
As the Data Center Site Lead, you will serve as the main accountable owner for all matters related to data center critical operations, working collaboratively with internal and external stakeholders (mainly colocation provider) to ensure operational excellence. You will work hand-in-hand with access management and security systems to adhere to Oracle's stringent data center security standards/policies. Additionally, you will actively involve in incident, change, and vendor management for data center space, cooling, and power systems. Your proactive approach to identifying and mitigating risks associated with data center operations will be vital to the success of this role.
Career Level - IC4
1. Process discipline — Must have
Candidate should be strong in data center operational processes, including SOP, MOP, EOP, SOO, change control, incident review, problem management, risk register management, corrective/preventive actions, audit readiness, and compliance tracking.
2. Technical expertise — Must have
Candidate should have strong working knowledge in at least one of the following areas: Mechanical systems, Electrical systems, TCS loop/liquid cooling, Project Management, Server & Network infrastructure, or Commissioning.

You do not need to be the deepest SME in every area, but should have enough technical understanding to challenge, validate, coordinate, and drive closure with Colo, DCFE, Design, NW, Security, Access Management, and other stakeholders.

3. Data center security practices — Must have
Candidate should understand data center security standards and be able to coordinate closely with Access Management, Security Systems, Colo, and internal stakeholders to ensure compliance with Oracle’s security policies, access control requirements, audit expectations, and site security procedures.
4. Business continuity and shift coverage — Must have
Candidate should understand 24x7 data center operational expectations, business continuity requirements, backup coverage, cross-training, shift planning, weekend/public holiday support, and escalation management. The role may require support outside normal business hours based on business needs.
5. Colo and stakeholder governance — Must have
Candidate should be able to collaborate effectively with colocation providers and internal stakeholders to maintain 100% data center availability. This includes leading weekly, monthly, and quarterly operations reviews, tracking action items, reviewing performance, and ensuring site-specific processes are established and followed.
6. Incident, change, problem, and risk management — Must have
Candidate should be able to lead and manage incidents, changes, and problems related to data center space, cooling, power, security, and operational readiness. The candidate should proactively identify risks, initiate corrective/preventive actions, and implement global or industry best practices where applicable.
7. Build-to-operations handover — Should have
Candidate should have knowledge of new data center build/deployment support, project-to-operations handover, operational readiness review, site acceptance, as-built documentation, open defect closure, handover checklist, and lessons learned from build-to-operations transition activities.
8. Team leadership and mentoring — Should have
Candidate should be able to oversee, guide, and mentor data center technicians and engineers while supporting team development, operational discipline, and ownership at site level.
9. Reporting, audit, and compliance — Should have
Candidate should be able to provide regular reports and audits on data center performance, security, risks, compliance status, open actions, and operational readiness.
10. Liquid cooling / TCS loop exposure — Good to have
Exposure to liquid cooling, TCS loop, GPU/high-density deployments, or related infrastructure will be an added advantage as Malaysia continues to scale with high-density workloads.
Oracle is seeking a Data Center Site Lead to oversee critical data center operations, ensuring the continuous availability, performance, security, and safety of the facility. The ideal candidate shall possess strong fundamentals in critical facilities operations, a proven commitment to maintaining 100% uptime for data center critical services, and the ability to uphold all data center security and safety compliance requirements.

jobs.description:
About the Role
Oracle is seeking a Supplier Sourcing Program Manager to support the sourcing and supply of data center fiber and optical components. This role will work closely with Engineering, Data Center Operations, Order Fulfillment, Procurement, and supplier partners to ensure materials and components are available to support Oracle's growing data center infrastructure.
The successful candidate will help manage supplier relationships, commercial negotiations, sourcing activities, supplier performance, and supply continuity. The role requires strong analytical and communication skills, an ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced and ambiguous environment, and a willingness to take ownership of complex supply-chain challenges.
